subject: Remote agent telemetry exports — DPA/dataflow clarifications
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@medinsight.io>

Cc: privacy@medinsight.io
Date: Sun, 7 Sep 2025 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Remote agent telemetry exports — initial questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will run inference via your remote agent installed on thin clients at healthcare partner sites. A few quick, urgent questions as we complete our DPA review and map telemetry in the SSQ (attached):

1) Which telemetry fields are exported off-agent by default? We're primarily concerned about any free-text fields that could contain PII (patient names, identifiers).
2) Are there built-in redaction or pseudonymization options for live telemetry prior to export?
3) How does retention work for remote-agent logs vs. hosted request traces under our DPA?
4) Can you confirm the subprocessor list for telemetry storage and analytics?

I've attached our completed SSQ template (medinsight_ssq_v2.xlsx) and a small sample schema (medinsight_sample_schema.csv). Can you map the rows in tab "TelemetryFields" to Redwood's internal names and indicate whether any field is considered PII by default?

We're on a tight timeline — would appreciate any clarifications before our legal sends the DPA back on Wednesday 9 Sep. Happy to do a short call if easier.

Best,
Marta Lopez
Privacy Lead, MedInsight
marta.lopez@medinsight.io

Attachments: medinsight_ssq_v2.xlsx, medinsight_sample_schema.csv
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@medinsight.io>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Sep 2025 10:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Remote agent telemetry exports — initial questions

Marta — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments, this helps. Looping in Laura (privacy) and Priyom (security) to confirm the DPA implications and mapping. Quick high-level answers from product/security: 

- Default exports: agent heartbeats (instance_id, status), CPU/memory metrics, anonymized histograms of request latencies, and aggregated model telemetry (token counts, model id). By default we do NOT export full user inputs or model outputs unless the customer enables request-logging.

- PII risk: fields that can contain PII only appear if request-logging is enabled. When enabled, customers can choose to mask or hash fields at the agent before export. We also support HMAC-based ID hashing with a customer-supplied key.

- Redaction/pseudonymization: agent config supports regex-based redaction rules (edge) and a binary toggle to hash user identifiers prior to export. We can provide a sample config that applies an email/name regex to the user_input field.

- Retention: remote-agent telemetry is retained per-customer settings. Default retention for transient telemetry is 30 days; request logs (if enabled) default to 90 days but can be shortened in the DPA addendum. Audit logs and security traces follow a separate retention SLA.

- Subprocessors: telemetry storage and analytics are handled by our analytics subprocessor (LogStream Inc.) and cloud object store (RedCloud Storage). We'll provide the current subprocessor roster and the SOC-2 excerpts you requested.

Next steps I'm proposing: Laura/ Priyom, can you review Marta's attached sheet and produce a two-column mapping (MedInsight field -> Redwood telemetry field) and mark PII:YES/NO? We'll also attach a sanitized dataflow diagram and a sanitized CSV sample. Marta — is a 30-min call on Tue 9 Sep at 15:00 UTC possible?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Marta / team — thanks for the patience. I've reviewed the attached SSQ and produced a concise mapping and guidance below. I'll upload a sanitized dataflow diagram (redwood_dataflow_diagram_v3.png) to the Drive link and drop a sanitized sample CSV in the thread by EOD. High-level summary: 

1) Mapping (select rows from TelemetryFields tab):
   - medinsight:client_instance_id -> redwood:agent_instance_id (non-PII, persistent GUID)
   - medinsight:user_id -> redwood:user_hash (PII if unhashed; default behavior: HMAC-SHA256 using customer key => PSEUDONYMOUS)
   - medinsight:user_input -> redwood:request_payload (NOT exported by default; exported only if request-logging enabled)
   - medinsight:error_trace -> redwood:error_logs (aggregated, stack traces truncated; no input payload)
   - medinsight:latency_ms -> redwood:latency_histogram (aggregated buckets)

2) PII approach & controls:
   - Default stance: no free-text user inputs leave the agent unless customer toggles. Identifiers are pseudonymized using HMAC if enabled. We recommend you enable agent-side masking for name/email regex and HMAC hashing for user IDs.
   - We support per-customer key provisioning so hashes are non-reversible by Redwood without the key (customer-managed key option available via KMS integration).

3) Retention & DPA language suggestions:
   - Suggested default clause: "Redwood will retain remote-agent telemetry for 30 days unless otherwise agreed in writing; customer request logs retention is configurable and may be reduced to 0 days on request."
   - We can add a DPA exhibit listing telemetry subprocessors and commit to providing exportable evidence (SOC2 summary + subprocessor list).

4) Subprocessors & evidence:
   - Current telemetry-related subprocessors: LogStream Inc. (analytics), RedCloud Storage (object store), TelemetryOps (support & alerting). We will provide SOC-2 Type II summaries and Data Processing Addendum exhibits within 3 business days for legal review.

5) Action items I will deliver by EOD Tue 9 Sep:
   - sanitized CSV mapping example (no real PII)
   - redwood_dataflow_diagram_v3.png (sanitized for public sharing)
   - recommended DPA clause text for retention and subprocessor disclosure

If anything in the mapping is unclear, call out the exact row ID in the SSQ and I will annotate. I'm also available for the 30-min call Karthik proposed at Tue 9 Sep 15:00 UTC — please confirm and I'll send an invite.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
